info.title: ouroboros-rest
info.summary: The public API of Ouroboros — the only boundary between the browser and everything behind it.
info.description:
The **communications layer** of
[Ouroboros](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros): the one service a browser talks
to. It owns authentication, sessions, tenant-context resolution, the tenancy API and
the gateway to `ouroboros-engine` — and it is the only module that reaches
`ouroboros-db` or the engine, which is what keeps tenancy enforcement in a single
auditable place.

**This document describes two families, and a client uses a different library for
each** ([#711](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/711)).

| Family | Paths | Called through |
|---|---|---|
| Auth | `/api/auth/*` — the `identity` and `organizations` tags | **BetterAuth's own client** (`createAuthClient`) |
| Everything else | `/api/v1/*` | **The client generated from this document** ([#43](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/43)) |

The split is not a preference. BetterAuth serves those routes itself, from a handler
mounted ahead of the router, and it ships a typed client that already knows their
bodies, their cookies and their error codes — so **the auth family is excluded from code
generation**, and calling it through a generated client would mean maintaining a second,
worse copy of something the library gives away. They are described here anyway, because
a client author has to be able to read them.

**Who is signed in is three calls, and not a fourth.** `GET /api/auth/get-session` is
the person, `GET /api/auth/organization/list` is the workspaces they belong to, and
`GET /api/auth/organization/get-active-member-role` is what they hold in one of them.
There is deliberately **no `/api/v1/auth/me`**: there was until #711, and it was deleted
rather than kept, because two routes answering *who is signed in* are two answers that
can disagree — and the one built over this service's own tables would be disagreeing
with the session the library actually resolved. Do not add another.

Every `/api/v1` path sits under that prefix. The version is in the URI because that is
what a generated client, an address bar and a log line can all carry without
negotiation, and a controller opts *out* of v1 rather than into it — so a route cannot
be published unversioned by omission. The auth family sits *beside* that prefix rather
than inside it, because the library versions its own routes and a second version number
in the path would be a promise this service is not the one keeping.

Two more paths are deliberately *not* under `/api/v1`: `/health/live` and `/health/ready`.
They are read by infrastructure with no notion of an API version — a container's
`HEALTHCHECK`, a compose healthcheck, an orchestrator's probe — and each of those is
configured once and must keep working when a version is added or retired, which is the
same reason `ouroboros-engine`'s liveness route is `/healthz` rather than
`/v0/healthz`. They are described here anyway, because this document describes
everything the service serves.

**Every error has one shape** — `{code, message, details}`, from every operation below
and from `ouroboros-engine` behind it (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.3). `code` is stable
and machine-readable and is what a client branches on; `message` is written for a
person; `details` carries what is specific to the failure, which for a `422` is one
entry per field that was refused. A constraint the database enforces is answered in the
same envelope rather than leaking through it: a duplicate domain is a `409` with
`code: "domain_taken"`, never a PostgreSQL error string.

**Lists are paginated the same way** — `?limit=&offset=`, answering
`{items, total, limit, offset}`. The window is echoed back so a client that sent
neither can still compute the next page, and `total` is always counted so a page count
can be rendered.

What is described below is the whole of the surface today: the heartbeat the scaffold
([#27](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/27)) landed, the probes
([#29](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/29)), the tenancy API
([#31](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/31)), the auth family BetterAuth
serves ([#701](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/701),
[#702](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/702),
[#704](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/704)) and the engine gateway
([#35](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/35)).

**Everything below requires a session** except the operations that carry
`security: []` — the routes a signed-out browser has to be able to reach at all (signing
in, the callback, reading a session that may be absent, signing out) and the three whose
reader is not a browser. A request without one is a `401` with
`code: "unauthenticated"`, and that is one answer covering every way a session can fail:
absent, expired, revoked, forged, or naming a person who no longer exists.

**Every `/api/v1` request also operates in one workspace**
([#32](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/32)). It is named by the
`{tenantId}` in the path, or by the `X-Ouro-Tenant` header on the operations that have
none, or inferred when the caller belongs to exactly one. A workspace the caller is not
a member of answers **`404`, never `403`** — a `403` would confirm that an identifier
names something real — and a member whose role is too low gets the one `403` this API
does answer, because by then the workspace is no secret from them.

servers.description:
`yarn dev`, which binds the loopback interface only — a development machine does
not answer to the network it is on. In a deployment the origin is whatever fronts
the service and the port comes from `PORT`; `4000` is the development default from
`docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § 4's port map.

tags.name: service
tags.description:
Identity and liveness — what answers before any contract does: the heartbeat, and the
two probes a container platform reads to decide whether to restart this process and
whether to send it traffic.

tags.name: identity
tags.description:
**Signing in, the session, and signing out — served by BetterAuth, called through
BetterAuth's client.**

These paths are the library's, not this service's
([#701](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/701)). It registers one handler
on the HTTP adapter ahead of Nest's router, so they never reach the routing table
`/api/v1` and URI versioning are applied to — which is why they sit beside that prefix
rather than inside it. `ouroboros-rest/src/auth/auth.routes.ts` is the map they are
published from, and `src/openapi/openapi.spec.ts` is what holds this section and that
map to each other.

**Call them with `createAuthClient`, not with the generated client.** They are
excluded from code generation, so a generated client has no method for any of them —
deliberately. See the two-client rule at the top of this document.

**Who is signed in is `get-session` plus the two organization routes** — never a
route of this service's own. `GET /api/v1/auth/me` existed until
[#711](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/711) and was deleted there: it
answered the same question from this service's own tables, which is one answer too
many.

**The session is a row, and signing out deletes it**
([#703](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/703)). Revocation is immediate:
a cookie copied before sign-out is refused on its next use rather than honoured for
the remainder of its week, which closes the revocation half of
[#38](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/38). BetterAuth holds the row and
the cookie; the lifetime and the cookie cache are in
`ouroboros-rest/src/auth/session.options.ts`, with the argument for every value, and
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 4.1.1 publishes them.

**The cookie changed name with the mechanism.** It was `ouro_session` and is now
BetterAuth's `better-auth.session_token`, which **invalidated every session live at
the cut-over** — there is no way to migrate a stateless signed cookie into a session
row, and inventing one would mean trusting the signature the change exists to stop
trusting. A browser still sending the old cookie is answered `401` and told to drop
it.

**A cross-origin caller must ask for its cookies** — `credentials: "include"` — and
its origin must be listed in `OURO_CORS_ORIGINS`. A credentialed request may not be
answered with a wildcard, so an origin that is not named is one whose sign-in appears
to succeed and whose next call is a `401`.

tags.name: organizations
tags.description:
**Workspaces, membership and roles — the tenancy backbone**
([#704](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/704), decision A5). BetterAuth's
organization plugin, so the same client and the same exclusion from codegen as
`identity` above.

An organization *is* a tenant. Which one a request operates in is
`session.activeOrganizationId` — **server state, set by `set-active`**, rather than a
header a client asserts. That is what mockup 01 Step 2's *Enter mission control →*
writes, and [#713](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/713) is what teaches
this service's own middleware to read it.

Four roles: `owner`, `admin`, `member` and the `viewer` this service adds as a custom
access-control role. `owner` and `admin` may administer an organization; `member` and
`viewer` may read it. The one nobody can grant is `owner` — it is what creating an
organization makes you.

**`list` carries no role, and that is the plugin's shape rather than an omission
here.** It reads the caller's `member` rows and returns the organizations they point
at. What you hold in one of them is `get-active-member-role`, which is a separate call
because it is a separate question — and because answering it for every organization at
once would mean reading every membership of each.

tags.name: auth
tags.description:
**This service's own auth routes — the `/api/v1` half, called through the generated
client.**

Two families share the word *auth* and it is worth being exact about which is which:
`identity` and `organizations` above are BetterAuth's, under `/api/auth`; this tag is
the versioned surface this service serves itself, under `/api/v1/auth`. Signing in,
the session and the organization operations are **not** here and must not be added
here — see the two-client rule at the top of this document.

One operation today. `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` is the versioned alias of BetterAuth's
`sign-out` and delegates to it rather than implementing a second one;
[#712](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/712) adds `POST /api/v1/auth/discover`,
the company-domain lookup behind mockup 01 Step 1, which is genuinely this service's
because it reads this service's tenant domains.

tags.name: engine
tags.description:
The gateway to `ouroboros-engine`, the Python backend that executes the work this
service brokers. It is internal — reachable from this service and from nothing else
(`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 10) — so everything a client learns about it, it learns
through an operation here.

There is no proxy route and there will not be one. Each engine capability arrives as a
named operation with its own contract in this document, because a route that forwarded
a path, a method and a body to an internal service would be that boundary written as a
hole.

**The engine failing is always a `502`.** Down, slow, unresolvable, holding a
mismatched shared secret, or answering outside its own contract are one answer with
one code, naming no address. A mismatched secret in particular is never forwarded as a
`401`: it is a deployment's mistake rather than a caller's, and telling a browser to
sign in again for it would be telling it about a boundary it cannot reach.

tags.name: tenants
tags.description:
Isolated customer workspaces — the root of everything else. A tenant has a slug that
appears in URLs and command arguments, a display name, and a lifecycle: `active`,
`suspended`, or the `deleted` that is a soft-delete marker rather than a removal.

**A workspace you are not a member of answers `404`, not `403`**
([#32](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/32)). A `403` would confirm that
an identifier names something real, which is the whole of what somebody enumerating
identifiers is trying to learn — so "no such workspace" and "not yours" are one
answer. `GET /api/v1/tenants` is scoped the same way: it lists the workspaces *you*
belong to, never the installation's.

Creating one makes you its `owner`, in the same transaction. Before the rule above
that was harmless; with it, a workspace with no members would be one nobody — its
creator included — could ever reach again.

There is deliberately no `DELETE`. A hard delete takes a tenant's domains, members,
organisations and repositories with it — every foreign key in the schema cascades —
and that is not an operation an HTTP verb should put one click away.

tags.name: domains
tags.description:
The email domains that resolve a tenant at sign-in. One tenant may present several;
at most one of them is the primary the product displays back, and zero is legal for a
tenant part-way through setting itself up.

A domain is globally unique: it names exactly one tenant, so a second tenant claiming
it is a `409` with `code: "domain_taken"`.

tags.name: members
tags.description:
Who belongs to a tenant, and what they may do there — `owner`, `admin`, `member` or
`viewer`. A member is addressed by the *person's* id, because a membership is the
`(tenant, person)` pair rather than a row with an identity of its own.

One rule here is enforced by this service rather than by the database, because it
spans rows and must survive both a role change and a removal: **a tenant always keeps
at least one owner.** Demoting or removing the last one is a `409` with
`code: "last_owner"`.

The roles are also what every mutation in this document is checked against: `owner`
and `admin` may change a workspace, `member` and `viewer` may read it. A member whose
role is too low gets a `403` with `code: "forbidden"` — the one place this API answers
`403`, because by then the caller has already proved the workspace is no secret from
them.

tags.name: github
tags.description:
The GitHub organisations and repositories a tenant has enabled — the boundary of where
Ouroboros may operate. Both carry their own flag, and a repository is in scope only
when **both** are true, so suspending an organisation preserves the per-repository
choices underneath it.

Both default to off. A row records that Ouroboros knows about the organisation or the
repository; the flag records that somebody deliberately turned it on.

get.description:
Report that the service is up, and which build is up.

Deliberately the same three questions `ouroboros-engine`'s `/v0/status` answers,
in the same order — *what is this*, *which build*, *how long has it been up* — so
someone looking at both services is reading one shape rather than two. It opens
no connection and reads no configuration: whether the service's *dependencies*
are reachable is a readiness probe's question
([#29](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/29)), not this one's.

200.description: The service is answering, and this is the build that answered.

post.description:
Start the GitHub handshake ([#702](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/702)).
`{"provider": "github"}` is the whole body; the answer carries the github.com
authorization URL for the browser to follow.

**A `POST` answering with a URL rather than a redirect**, so a script can decide what
to do with it — which is why `ouroboros-ui` calls `authClient.signIn.social` instead
of rendering a link. An anchor pointed at this path gets a `404`: it does not answer
`GET`.

`github` is the only provider configured, plus email/password in development
([#705](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/705)). The scopes are
`read:user` and `user:email` and are this service's rather than the library's
defaults — see `src/auth/github.provider.ts`.

200.description:
The authorization URL to send the browser to. `redirect` is `true` unless the
caller asked for none, in which case a `Location` header is also set.

400.description:
The provider is unknown or not configured. BetterAuth's error shape, not this
API's envelope — the library answers its own routes.

get.description:
Where the provider returns the browser. **This is the URL an OAuth App is registered
against** — `${BETTER_AUTH_URL}/api/auth/callback/github` — and github.com compares
what it was registered with against what the exchange presents, so a difference of
one character is a sign-in that fails at the last hop.

The library checks the `state` it issued, exchanges the code for the profile and the
verified primary address, upserts `"user"` and `account`, creates the `session` row
and sets its cookies. Nothing here is this service's to call: it is a navigation the
browser makes.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The value issued when the sign-in began, echoed back for checking.

302.description:
Signed in, and back to the application. `Set-Cookie` carries the session token
and its cache.

Location.description: Where the browser is sent next — the application, or `/api/auth/error`.

post.description:
The same operation for a provider that returns by form post rather than by
redirect. GitHub redirects, so this is the verb nothing in this installation uses —
described because the library answers it and a document that described half a route
would be describing something else.

get.description:
The caller's session and the person holding it, or `null` for nobody.

**This is the only route that answers *who is signed in*.** `GET /api/v1/auth/me`
answered it too until [#711](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/711)
deleted it; do not build another. The two questions it also used to answer are
`GET /api/auth/organization/list` (where do I belong) and
`GET /api/auth/organization/get-active-member-role` (what may I do here).

`null` rather than a `401`, which is what makes it callable from a login screen: the
absence of a session is the answer, not a failure. Since
[#703](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/703) the global guard calls it on
every request, and with the cookie cache fresh it answers from the signed snapshot in
`better-auth.session_data` and issues no statement at all.

`session.activeOrganizationId` is the tenant pointer — see the `organizations` tag.

200.description: The session and its user, or `null` when the request carries neither.

post.description:
The same answer for a caller that would rather not put anything in a URL. Identical
in every respect; the library accepts both verbs.

End the session and clear its cookies. **It deletes the `session` row**
([#703](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/703)), so revocation is
immediate rather than an expiry a copied cookie can outlive.

`POST /api/v1/auth/logout` is this service's versioned alias and delegates here; the
two are interchangeable, and which one a client calls is decided by which client it
is calling through.

200.description: Signed out. The cookies are emptied with `Max-Age=0`.

get.description:
`{"ok": true}` — no database, no session, no configuration read.

**It is not a health probe.** It says the BetterAuth handler is mounted and nothing
else: not that the database is reachable, not that the engine is. `/health/ready` is
the readiness answer and this is deliberately not a second one.

Where the library redirects a browser whose sign-in failed, with the reason in the
query string. It answers HTML for a person to read rather than JSON for a client to
parse, because whoever arrives here arrived by navigation.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: The reason the flow failed, as the library names it.

get.description:
Every organization the caller is a member of — mockup 01 Step 2's list, and
mockup 17's. `metadata.personal` is what renders the `personal` pill
([#704](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/704)).

It answers **from the session**, so there is no id to pass and no way to ask about
somebody else's memberships.

**It carries no role.** The plugin reads the caller's `member` rows and returns the
organizations they point at, discarding the role on the way — so *what may I do
here* is `get-active-member-role`, a separate call because it is a separate
question.

200.description: The caller's organizations. Empty for somebody invited nowhere yet.

401.description: No session. BetterAuth's error shape, not this API's envelope.

post.description:
The caller becomes its `owner` — the one role nobody else can grant — and it becomes
the session's active organization unless `keepCurrentActiveOrganization` says
otherwise.

**A `personal` flag in `metadata` is stripped before the row is written.** The pill
it would render means *this workspace is yours alone*, and a shared workspace wearing
it would be a label that lies on the one screen whose job is to say where somebody's
work is going. A personal organization is made by first sign-in and by nothing else —
see `stripPersonalFlag` in `src/auth/organization.plugin.ts`.

200.description: The organization, with the caller's own membership row.

400.description: The slug is already taken, or the body did not validate.

401.description: No session.

post.description:
Mockup 01 Step 2's **Enter mission control →**. It **writes
`session.activeOrganizationId`**, which is what makes the tenant server state rather
than a header a client asserts (decision A5), and
[#713](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/713) is what teaches this
service's own middleware to read it.

Name the organization by id or by slug. `null` unsets the pointer, which is the
state somebody who has signed in and chosen nothing yet is in.

200.description:
The organization now active, with its members and pending invitations — or
`null` when the pointer was unset.

403.description:
The caller is not a member of it. The pointer is cleared on the way out, so a
session cannot be left pointing somewhere it may not go.

get.summary: One workspace, with its members and invitations
get.description:
Mockup 17's members & roles table. Defaults to the session's active organization
when neither query parameter is given, and answers `null` when there is no active
one to default to.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: Which organization. Defaults to the session's active one.

parameters.name: organizationSlug
parameters.description: The same, by slug. Takes precedence over `organizationId`.

200.description: The organization, or `null` when there is no active one.

403.description: The caller is not a member of it.

get.description:
`{"role": "owner"}` for the session's active organization, or for whichever
`organizationId` names, provided the caller belongs to it.

**The third part of the session question**, and the reason `GET /api/v1/auth/me` was
deleted rather than reimplemented
([#711](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/711)): who you are is
`get-session`, where you belong is `organization/list`, and what you hold there is
this. Cheaper than `get-full-organization` for the purpose, and it discloses one role
rather than a whole membership list.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: Which organization. Defaults to the session's active one.

200.description: The role the caller holds there.

400.description: No such organization, or no active one to default to.

403.description: The caller is not a member of it.

post.description:
Writes an `invitation` row at the role given, and nothing else in MVP: **no email is
sent**. [#724](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/724) is the delivery, and
`expiresAt` is already on the row waiting for it
([#707](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/707)).

Requires the `invitation: create` permission, which `owner` and `admin` hold and
`member` and `viewer` do not — see `src/auth/organization.roles.ts`.

400.description: The address is already a member, or the body did not validate.

403.description:
The caller's role does not carry `invitation: create` — `member` and `viewer`
do not.

post.description:
Requires `member: update`, which `owner` and `admin` hold; `member` and `viewer` do
not, and `viewer` holds none of the four resources at all. This is the route
[#715](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/715) verifies a member-level
caller is refused on.

200.description: The membership, as it now stands.

400.description: No such member, or the body did not validate.

403.description:
The caller's role does not carry `member: update` — `member` and `viewer` do
not.

post.description:
End the session, and remove its cookies from the browser.

**It deletes the session row** ([#703](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/703)),
so revocation is immediate: a cookie copied beforehand is refused on its next use.
This service delegates to BetterAuth's own `POST /api/auth/sign-out` rather than
implementing a second sign-out beside it, and the two are interchangeable — this
one is the versioned alias `ouroboros-ui` calls.

Idempotent, and reachable without a session: requiring one would mean an *expired*
cookie could never be cleared, because the request to remove it would be refused
for carrying exactly the thing it was trying to remove. It answers `204` either
way.

A `POST` rather than a `GET`, because it changes state — a `GET` that signs you out
is a link, an image tag or a prefetch away from signing you out.

It ends **one** session rather than all of the person's: somebody signing out of a
shared machine is not signed out of their own.

204.description:
Signed out. `Set-Cookie` removes the session cookie and its cache. There is no
body — there is nothing to say.

Set-Cookie.description:
`better-auth.session_token` and `better-auth.session_data`, emptied, with
`Max-Age=0` — one header each.

500.description:
`internal_error` — the service itself failed. The message is a constant and
`details` is empty, deliberately: the real diagnosis names a query, a host or a
role, and it goes to the service log where only an operator reads it.

get.summary: Report the engine's health and version
get.description:
Whether `ouroboros-engine` is reachable, and which build answered.

The engine is internal — it is reachable from this service and from nothing else
(`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 10) — so this is how a signed-in person learns anything
about it at all. This service asks the engine `GET /v0/status` over the internal
boundary, carrying a shared secret a browser never sees, and reports back the two
facts a caller can act on.

**Every way that call can fail is one `502`.** An engine that is down, one that is
too slow, one at an address that no longer resolves, one holding a different shared
secret, and one answering outside its own contract are indistinguishable here by
design: the caller learns that the system cannot serve the request, and nothing it
could use to probe the inside of the network. In particular a shared-secret mismatch
is **never** forwarded as a `401` — that is this deployment's mistake rather than the
caller's, and it is logged where an operator reads it.

This route is not a proxy. It is a named operation with its own contract that
happens to be answered by asking the engine one question, because a route that
forwarded a path, a method and a body to an internal service would be the boundary
above written as a hole.

401.description:
`unauthenticated` — this request carries no session, or one this service will
not honour. The engine's own credential has nothing to do with this answer; see
the `502` below.

500.description:
`internal_error` — the service itself failed. The message is a constant and
`details` is empty, deliberately: the real diagnosis names a query, a host or a
role, and it goes to the service log where only an operator reads it.

502.description:
`engine_unavailable` — the engine could not serve this request. `details` is
empty and the message names no address: everything that would go in them — the
status the engine answered, the code the socket failed with, the URL that was
called — is in this service's log instead.

A `502` rather than a `500`, because nothing in this service is broken and
retrying is reasonable.

example.message: The engine is not available right now. Try again in a moment.

get.description:
One page of the workspaces the signed-in person belongs to, oldest first.

**Scoped to the caller**, never the installation's whole table: a listing that
enumerated every workspace would be a larger existence leak than the `403` this API
answers `404` to avoid, and it would be one request rather than a scan. Somebody who
belongs to none gets an empty page.

It is one of the three operations that need no active workspace, and the reason is
circularity: this is the question a workspace switcher asks *before* it can name
one.

Ordered by creation time and then by id. The second term is not decoration: two
tenants created in the same millisecond would otherwise be free to swap places
between requests, and a paginated read could show one of them twice and the other
never.

401.description:
`unauthenticated` — this request carries no session, or one this service will
not honour. Sign in through `/api/auth/sign-in/social`.

Every way a session can fail is this one answer: absent, expired, signed with a
rotated key, forged, or naming a person who has since been deleted. A client

get.description:
Report that the process is up and serving.

Deliberately shallow — it opens no connection, reads no configuration and calls
nothing downstream, so it cannot fail for a reason that has nothing to do with
whether this process should be restarted. Reaching the handler at all is the answer;
the three empty sections in the body are the shape `/health/ready` fills in.

Its reader restarts the container when this stops answering, which is why *no*
dependency is consulted here: a liveness probe that failed because PostgreSQL was
down would restart every replica of a healthy service, repeatedly, while the
database was the thing that needed attention.

Report whether this service's dependencies are reachable: PostgreSQL, asked
`SELECT 1` on a connection of the probe's own, and `ouroboros-engine`, asked for the
one route it serves without the internal key — `GET /healthz`.

Both are asked concurrently and reported independently, so a body that says the
database is down still says whether the engine is up. Every wait is bounded at two
seconds, so this answers whether or not a dependency does.

A `down` message names what was attempted and classifies why it failed. It carries
no host, no port, no role and no driver text: this route answers without
authentication, and the driver's own message — which is written for an operator and
names all three — goes to the service log instead.

Its reader takes the process out of rotation, or holds a dependent container back,
and putting it back costs nothing. That is why this one is allowed to fail because a
dependency is missing, and `/health/live` is not.

503.description:
At least one dependency did not answer. `error` names which, and `details` still
reports the ones that did.

ouroSession.name: better-auth.session_token
ouroSession.description:
The session cookie BetterAuth issues, removed by `/api/v1/auth/logout`. `HttpOnly`,
`SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`, seven days, and `Secure` over HTTPS — where it is also
named `__Secure-better-auth.session_token`, the library adding the prefix a browser
refuses to accept over plain HTTP.

**It replaced `ouro_session` in
[#703](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/703)**, which invalidated every
session live at the cut-over. A browser still holding the old cookie is answered
`401` and told to drop it.

It names a row in the `session` table — not a bearer token to be minted or pasted,
and not a claim about who you are. `apiKey`/`cookie` is OpenAPI's nearest
description of a cookie credential; it does not mean a client may compose one.

A second cookie, `better-auth.session_data`, travels beside it: a signed snapshot of
the session with a five-minute lifetime, which is what keeps an authenticated
request from costing a database lookup. Nothing sends it deliberately and no client
reads it.

A browser sends it automatically. A cross-origin caller must also ask for it —
`credentials: "include"` in `fetch` — and its origin must be listed in
`OURO_CORS_ORIGINS`, because a credentialed cross-origin request may not be
answered with a wildcard.

DomainId.name: domainId
DomainId.description: The domain's id. It must belong to the tenant in the path.

UserId.name: userId
UserId.description:
The person's id. A membership is the `(tenant, person)` pair rather than a row with
an identity of its own, so this is what addresses one.

OrgLogin.name: login
OrgLogin.description:
The organisation's GitHub login — the `NobuData` in github.com/NobuData, lower-cased.
GitHub treats logins case-insensitively, so they are stored folded and one casing is
the only one that resolves.

RepoName.name: name
RepoName.description:
The repository's name within its organisation, without the owner prefix — the
`ouroboros` in NobuData/ouroboros, lower-cased.

AuthProviderId.name: id
AuthProviderId.description:
The provider's name, as BetterAuth knows it. `github` is the only one configured, so
the callback github.com is registered against is `/api/auth/callback/github` — a
string three places have to agree on, and only one of them is code
(`GITHUB_CALLBACK_PATH` in `src/auth/auth.routes.ts`).

TenantHeader.name: X-Ouro-Tenant
TenantHeader.description:
The workspace this request is operating in — its slug or its uuid.

On the operations below it is **optional and redundant**: they already name a
workspace in their path, which is the more specific of the two, and a header that
names a *different* one is a `422` with `code: "tenant_mismatch"` rather than a
silent preference for either. It is accepted here so that one client can set it on
every request, and it is how the operations that have no workspace in their path —
everything the epic adds after this one — say which workspace they mean.

A caller who belongs to exactly one workspace may omit it everywhere; theirs is
inferred. A caller who belongs to several, on an operation with no `{tenantId}`,
gets a `422` with `code: "tenant_required"`.

slug.summary: By slug — what a person types

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description:
How many rows to return. The ceiling is not a suggestion: without it, a `limit` of a
million is a client's way of asking this service to hold a table in memory, and the
request that does it is indistinguishable from a mistake in a loop.

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
The body of **every** error this API answers with, and the same shape
`ouroboros-engine` uses behind it (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.3). A failure the
framework produced — a path no route claims, a body the parser refused — carries it
too, so a client has one thing to parse rather than one per layer.

code.description:
Stable, machine-readable, and the thing to branch on. Every code this API can
answer with is named in the description of the response that carries it.

message.description:
Written for a person. It may name a value the caller sent and never names
anything about the service's own internals — no driver text, no stack, no
constraint. A `500`'s message is a constant for exactly that reason.
examples: That domain belongs to another tenant.

details.description:
Whatever is specific to this failure — the field messages of a `422`, keyed by
field path; the identifier a `404` was asked about; the constraint a generic
conflict tripped. Always present, empty rather than absent when there is nothing
to add, so a client reading `details.x` never has to check `details` first.

slug: slug must be lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens

SignInSocialRequest.title: SignInSocialRequest
SignInSocialRequest.description: Which provider to sign in with, and where to come back to.

provider.description:
The provider's id. `github` is the only one configured — see
`src/auth/github.provider.ts`.

callbackURL.description: Where to send the browser once the handshake completes.

errorCallbackURL.description: Where to send it when the handshake fails, instead of `/api/auth/error`.

disableRedirect.description:
Answer with the URL only, setting no `Location` header. `ouroboros-ui` follows
the URL itself, which is what makes the sign-in button a script's decision
rather than a navigation the service forces.

SignInSocialResponse.title: SignInSocialResponse
SignInSocialResponse.description: Where to send the browser to authorize.

url.description: The provider's authorization URL, carrying the `state` this service issued.

redirect.description: Whether a `Location` header was set beside the body.

AuthUser.title: AuthUser
AuthUser.description:
The signed-in person, as BetterAuth holds them — the `"user"` table
([#706](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/706)).

One human is one row however many organizations they belong to. `name` and `image`
are the library's field names; this API's own resources call the same two things
`displayName` and `avatarUrl`.

id.description:
Stable for the person's whole life. A uuid rendered as text for everybody who
came across in V004's back-fill, and the library's own id for anybody who signed
in after it.

email.description:
Lower-cased and unique. How a person is recognised — including as the recipient
of an invitation sent before they ever signed in — and not how they
authenticate.

emailVerified.description:
Whether *this service* has verified the address. Not what authorises account
linking: that needs the **provider** to call it verified, which is the stricter
of the two — see `ACCOUNT_LINKING` in `src/auth/github.provider.ts`.

name.description: Their name on GitHub, or their login when they have set none.

image.description: The avatar the provider hosts, or `null` — which is what makes the UI draw a monogram.

AuthSession.title: AuthSession
AuthSession.description:
The session row itself. **A row, not a claim in a cookie** — which is what makes
sign-out immediate and a deleted account's outstanding session stop working at once
([#703](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/703)).

userId.description: The person this session belongs to.

token.description:
The value the session cookie carries. Published because the shape has it, not
because a client should read it: the cookie is `HttpOnly` and nothing in a
browser can.

activeOrganizationId.description:
**The tenant pointer** — which organization this session is acting in, or `null`
for somebody who has signed in and chosen nothing yet. Written by
`POST /api/auth/organization/set-active` and by nothing a client can assert
(decision A5).

AuthSessionEnvelope.title: AuthSessionEnvelope
AuthSessionEnvelope.description: What `get-session` answers when there is a session to answer with.

AuthSessionOrNull.title: AuthSessionOrNull
AuthSessionOrNull.description:
The session, or `null` for nobody.

`null` rather than a `401`, and that is the property a login screen is built on: it
has to be able to ask *is anybody signed in* and get an answer rather than a
redirect.

SignOutResponse.title: SignOutResponse
SignOutResponse.description:
`{"success": true}`, whether or not there was a session to end — the removal is
idempotent, because requiring a live session to clear an expired cookie would mean
the cookie could never be cleared.

AuthOk.title: AuthOk
AuthOk.description: The BetterAuth handler answering for itself, and for nothing else.

AuthError.title: AuthError
AuthError.description:
**BetterAuth's error shape, which is not this API's envelope.** The `/api/v1` routes
answer `{code, message, details}` from one filter; these routes are the library's
and it composes its own failures, so a client handling both families handles two
error shapes. That is a real cost of the two-client rule, and stating it is cheaper
than a client discovering it.

examples: You are not a member of this organization

code.description: The library's stable code, screaming case.

MemberRole.title: MemberRole
MemberRole.description:
What somebody may do in an organization. Three are the plugin's; `viewer` is this
service's, added as a custom access-control role so the vocabulary
`V002__users_membership.sql` had been storing since
[#21](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/21) survived the move
(`src/auth/organization.roles.ts`).

MemberRoleResponse.title: MemberRoleResponse
MemberRoleResponse.description: The role the caller holds in one organization.

Organization.title: Organization
Organization.description:
A workspace — the tenancy backbone since
[#704](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/704). What `V001__tenants.sql`
called a `tenant`, holding the same ids: `V006__tenancy_extensions.sql` moved the
rows across without remapping them ([#708](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/708)).

id.description: Stable for the organization's whole life. The slug is not; this is what to store.

slug.description: The URL- and CLI-safe handle, unique across the installation.

metadata.description:
`{"personal": true}` is the one key this installation writes, and it is what
renders mockup 01 Step 2's `personal` pill. **A client cannot set it**: it is
stripped from every creation request, so the pill can only ever be telling the
truth.

OrganizationMember.title: OrganizationMember
OrganizationMember.description:
One person's membership of one organization — the `(organization, person)` pair, and
the role they hold in it.

createdAt.description:
When the membership came into being. The plugin keeps one timestamp where
`tenant_members` kept two, so *invited* and *joined* are no longer separable —
an invitation lives on the `invitation` row until it is accepted, and the member
row is written at acceptance.

user.description: The person, when the caller asked for a listing that joins them in.

Invitation.title: Invitation
Invitation.description:
Somebody asked to join, at a role, before they are a member.

**No email is sent in MVP** — the row is the whole of the operation, and
[#724](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/724) is the delivery. `expiresAt`
is already here waiting for it.

email.description: Who was invited. They need not have an account yet.

FullOrganization.title: FullOrganization
FullOrganization.description:
One organization with its people — mockup 17's members & roles table in a single
answer.

FullOrganizationOrNull.title: FullOrganizationOrNull
FullOrganizationOrNull.description:
The organization, or `null` — which is what a session with no active organization
gets, rather than an error. Choosing nothing yet is a state the login screen exists
to resolve, not a failure.

CreatedOrganization.title: CreatedOrganization
CreatedOrganization.description:
The new organization, with the caller's own membership — the `owner` row created in
the same operation, so nothing has to be read back to find out what they hold.

CreateOrganizationRequest.title: CreateOrganizationRequest
CreateOrganizationRequest.description: A workspace to create. The caller becomes its `owner`.

slug.description: Unique across the installation; a taken one is a `400`.

metadata.description:
**`personal` is stripped from whatever is sent here.** See the operation's own
description for why the one flag a client may not set is the one that renders a
pill.

keepCurrentActiveOrganization.description:
Create it without switching into it. Absent means the new organization becomes
the session's active one, which is what somebody creating their first workspace
wants.

SetActiveOrganizationRequest.title: SetActiveOrganizationRequest
SetActiveOrganizationRequest.description:
Which organization this session acts in. Give an id or a slug; give `null` to unset
the pointer.

OrgInviteMemberRequest.title: OrgInviteMemberRequest
OrgInviteMemberRequest.description: Somebody to invite, and what they will hold when they accept.

organizationId.description: Which organization. Defaults to the session's active one.

resend.description: Re-issue an outstanding invitation rather than refusing a duplicate.

UpdateMemberRoleRequest.title: UpdateMemberRoleRequest
UpdateMemberRoleRequest.description: A membership, and the role it should now hold.

memberId.description: The membership row's id — not the person's.

organizationId.description: Which organization. Defaults to the session's active one.

Tenant.title: Tenant
Tenant.description: An isolated customer workspace — the root of everything else in the API.

id.description: Stable for the tenant's whole life. The slug is not; this is what to store.

slug.description:
The URL- and CLI-safe handle, unique across the installation. DNS-label shaped,
which keeps it usable if one is ever wanted as a subdomain.

displayName.description: What a human reads. Free text; it carries no machine meaning.

status.description:
The lifecycle. `deleted` is a soft-delete marker: the row and everything
cascading from it survive, so it is recoverable.

updatedAt.description: Maintained by the database on every write; never accepted from a client.

items.description: The rows for this window, oldest first.

total.description: How many rows there are in total, ignoring the window.

limit.description: The window that was applied — the default, when the request named none.

Domain.title: Domain
Domain.description: An email domain that resolves a tenant at sign-in.

domain.description:
Lower-cased, and unique across the whole installation rather than within the
tenant — a domain names exactly one tenant at sign-in.

isPrimary.description:
The domain the product displays back. At most one per tenant, and zero is legal
for a tenant part-way through setting itself up.

DomainPage.title: DomainPage
DomainPage.description: One page of a tenant's domains, the primary first.

Member.title: Member
Member.description:
A person's membership of one tenant, with the person's own details alongside — one
row of a member table.

Flattened rather than nested, and with no id of its own: the membership *is* the
`(tenantId, userId)` pair, which is what a `PATCH` or a `DELETE` addresses.

email.description:
Lower-cased and unique across the installation. How a person is recognised and
contacted — not how they authenticate.

displayName.description:
What the member list prints. For somebody who has never signed in this is the
name their inviter gave, or the local part of their address.

avatarUrl.description:
An `http(s)` URL, or `null` when none is known — which is every person who has
not signed in yet. A placeholder is the UI's decision, so none is invented here.

role.description: What this person may do in this tenant.

invitedAt.description: When the invitation was issued. Also when the membership came into being.

joinedAt.description:
When it was accepted, or `null` while it is outstanding — a real state the member
list renders, and what an invitation looks like until #33's sign-in exists.

MemberPage.title: MemberPage
MemberPage.description: One page of a tenant's members, by name.

Org.title: Org
Org.description: A GitHub organisation a tenant has recorded, enabled or not.

login.description: Lower-cased GitHub login, unique within the tenant.

enabled.description:
Whether Ouroboros may operate in it. A row records that the organisation is
known; this records that somebody deliberately turned it on.

installedAt.description:
When the GitHub App was installed. `null` on every row today — the installation
flow is future product work, and a default would assert something that never
happened.

OrgPage.title: OrgPage
OrgPage.description: One page of a tenant's GitHub organisations, by login.

Repo.title: Repo
Repo.description:
A repository within an organisation. In scope for Ouroboros only when this `enabled`
and its organisation's are **both** true.

orgId.description:
The organisation it hangs from. The tenant is reachable through that, and a
second copy of the fact here could disagree with it.

name.description: Lower-cased, without the owner prefix. Unique within the organisation.

enabled.description: Independent of the organisation's flag, so suspending one preserves this.

defaultBranch.description:
The branch work is cut from, or `null` until it has been discovered from GitHub.
An enable/disable that omits it leaves it alone rather than clearing it.

RepoPage.title: RepoPage
RepoPage.description: One page of an organisation's repositories, by name.

CreateTenantRequest.title: CreateTenantRequest
CreateTenantRequest.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/tenants`.

Request schemas are closed, as the response schemas are: a property this document
does not list is refused rather than ignored, which is what closes mass assignment
for every route at once instead of per handler.

UpdateTenantRequest.title: UpdateTenantRequest
UpdateTenantRequest.description:
The body of `PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}`. Every field optional; a body naming
none of them is a no-op that answers with the tenant unchanged.

domain.description:
Lower-cased. An address with upper case in it is refused rather than folded —
folding would mean the value stored is not the value sent, which is the beginning
of a client that cannot predict what a `GET` returns.

isPrimary.description: Make this the displayed domain, demoting whichever one holds it now.

UpdateDomainRequest.title: UpdateDomainRequest
UpdateDomainRequest.description:
The body of `PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/domains/{domainId}`. One field, because
it is the only thing about a domain that can change: the domain itself is what the
row *is*, and renaming one is adding the new and removing the old.

email.description:
Who to invite. Lower-cased before the lookup — the one value this API normalises
rather than refuses, because an address is typed by a person into a form and
`Ada@acme.example` is not a mistake worth an error message.

displayName.description:
What to call them if this is the first Ouroboros has heard of them. Ignored when
the person already exists — their own name is not an inviter's to overwrite.
Omitted, the local part of the address is used.

enabled.description:
Off unless asked. Anything arriving by a path nobody has thought about yet
arrives switched off, which is the right posture for a flag whose whole job is to
bound what an autonomous agent may touch.

UpdateRepoRequest.title: UpdateRepoRequest
UpdateRepoRequest.description:
The body of `PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/orgs/{login}/repos/{name}`, which is
also how a repository is first recorded.

defaultBranch.description:
The branch work is cut from. Left alone when omitted rather than cleared. The
shape is an allow-list — letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen and slash, with
no leading or trailing slash, no empty segment, no leading dot and no `..`
anywhere — because the value is joined onto a filesystem path.

engine.description:
Always `up`, and that is honest rather than redundant: every way the engine can
fail to answer is a `502`, so a body that exists at all came from a reachable
engine. It is a field rather than nothing so the shape can grow a second state —
`degraded`, once there is something that could be degraded — without changing how
a client reads the first one.

version.description:
The engine build that answered, read from its package metadata. It is the
engine's version and not this service's: the two are released independently
(`docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § 8), and which pair is deployed together is exactly what
this route exists to tell you.

service.description: This service's name, constant across deployments.

version.description:
The running build, read from this module's `package.json` — the one place a
module's version is written down (`docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § 8), and the same
string `info.version` above carries.

status.description:
Always `ok`. Reaching this handler at all is what the field reports; a client
reads the status code, and this is for the human who runs the request by
hand.

uptimeSeconds.description:
Seconds since the service was constructed, to millisecond precision. Small
and shrinking across polls means something is restarting the process — which
is the one thing a heartbeat can tell you that a plain `200` cannot.

HealthReport.title: HealthReport
HealthReport.description:
The body of both probes — one shape, so a reader parses one thing.

It is `@nestjs/terminus`'s report, and the three sections are the same dependencies
seen three ways: `info` holds the ones that are up, `error` the ones that are down,
and `details` holds all of them. All three are always present, and all three are
empty for `/health/live`, which has no dependencies to report on.

status.description:
`ok` when every dependency answered, `error` when one did not — and
`shutting_down` when the process has been told to stop, at which point it should
neither be sent traffic nor be counted live.

error.description: The dependencies that did not, each with a reason.

DependencyStatuses.title: DependencyStatuses
DependencyStatuses.description:
Dependencies, keyed by name. `/health/ready` reports two of them — `database` and
`engine` — and the map is open because a dependency added later is a key added here
rather than a new shape.

DependencyStatus.title: DependencyStatus
DependencyStatus.description: What one dependency reported when it was asked.

message.description:
Present when the status is `down`: what was attempted, and a classification of
why it failed — `SELECT 1 failed (ECONNREFUSED)`, `GET /healthz responded 503`,
`SELECT 1 timed out after 2000 ms`. Never a driver's own message; this route
answers without authentication, and a driver names the host, the port and the
role it could not reach with.
